title: Comparable monotone maps give a prism homotopy on augmented strict poset chains
statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative ring and $P,Q$ finite partially ordered sets, possibly empty. Write $C(P;R)$ for the chain complex of $R$-modules [def-weil-pbc-module-chain-complex-homology] whose degree $n\geq0$ is free on strict chains $[x_0<\cdots<x_n]$ in $P$, whose degree $-1$ is $R$ on $[\varnothing]$, and whose lower degrees are zero. Its differential is alternating vertex deletion, including $d[x]=[\varnothing]$ in degree zero and $d[\varnothing]=0$. In formulas, a weakly increasing tuple with a repeated entry denotes zero. For every monotone map $u:P\to Q$, the rule $u_*[x_0<\cdots<x_n]=[u(x_0)\leq\cdots\leq u(x_n)]$ and $u_*[\varnothing]=[\varnothing]$ defines a chain map $C(P;R)\to C(Q;R)$. These chain maps preserve identities and composition. If $f,g:P\to Q$ are monotone with $f(x)\leq g(x)$ for every $x$, the $R$-linear maps
$$h_n[x_0<\cdots<x_n]=\sum_{i=0}^n(-1)^i[f(x_0)\leq\cdots\leq f(x_i)\leq g(x_i)\leq\cdots\leq g(x_n)]\quad(n\geq0),\qquad h_{-1}=0$$
(and zero in lower degrees) satisfy $dh+hd=g_*-f_*$ in every integer degree.

proof.text: For a poset $S$, let $W_n(S)$ be the free $R$-module on weakly increasing tuples $(x_0,\ldots,x_n)$ for $n\geq0$, with $W_{-1}(S)=R[\varnothing]$ and zero below $-1$. Define $d$ by alternating deletion and $d[x]=[\varnothing]$. For positions $a<b$, deleting $a$ then the original $b$ has coefficient $(-1)^{a+b-1}$, whereas deleting $b$ then $a$ has coefficient $(-1)^{a+b}$; the resulting tuples agree. These pairs exhaust $d^2$ for $n\geq2$. For $n=1$, $d^2[x_0,x_1]=[\varnothing]-[\varnothing]=0$, and for $n\leq0$ the next differential is zero. Thus $W(S)$ is a chain complex in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-module-chain-complex-homology].

source.place: Tag 019S, lemma-homotopy-s-N, preceding equation-homotopy-to-homotopy (lines 4739–4846); explicit agent adaptation to weak tuples, quotient by repetitions, and augmentation.

proof.text: Let $D_n(S)\subseteq W_n(S)$ be spanned by tuples with a repetition, and put $D_n(S)=0$ for $n\leq0$. A repeated weak tuple has adjacent equal entries $x_j=x_{j+1}$: any equality at separated positions forces all intervening entries equal by antisymmetry. Deleting position $j$ or $j+1$ gives identical tuples with opposite coefficients; every other deletion retains these two adjacent equal entries. Hence $dD_n\subseteq D_{n-1}$. The quotient $W_n/D_n$ is identified with the free module on strict tuples by killing repeated basis tuples and keeping strict ones: this map and inclusion of strict generators are inverse after taking the quotient. In degree $-1$ it is the identity of $R$. The induced differential is exactly that of $C(S;R)$, so this also verifies the complex specified in the statement.

source.place: Tag 019S, lemma-homotopy-s-N, preceding equation-homotopy-to-homotopy (lines 4739–4846); explicit agent adaptation to weak tuples, quotient by repetitions, and augmentation.

proof.text: For a monotone $u:P\to Q$, entrywise application defines $W(u)_n$ on each free basis and is the identity in degree $-1$. It commutes with each vertex deletion, so $dW(u)=W(u)d$ in degrees $n\geq1$; in degree zero both composites send every vertex to $[\varnothing]$, and below zero both are zero. Equal adjacent entries have equal images, so $W(u)D(P)\subseteq D(Q)$. Therefore it induces a chain map on $W/D=C$, exactly $u_*$ from the statement; the termwise commutation is precisely the chain-map condition of [def-weil-pbc-module-chain-complex-homology].

proof.text: Entrywise identity fixes every tuple and the empty generator. For monotone $u:P\to Q$, $v:Q\to S$, entrywise $(v\circ u)$ equals successive entrywise application of $u$ and $v$, including in degree $-1$. These equalities pass to the quotients, giving $(\mathrm{id}_P)_*=\mathrm{id}_{C(P;R)}$ and $(v\circ u)_*=v_*u_*$. In particular, if $u$ collapses a strict tuple to a repeated tuple, every further image is still repeated, in agreement with the zero convention.

source.place: Tag 019S, lemma-homotopy-s-N, preceding equation-homotopy-to-homotopy (lines 4739–4846); explicit agent adaptation to weak tuples, quotient by repetitions, and augmentation.

proof.text: For a weak tuple $x=(x_0,\ldots,x_n)$ put $T_i(x)=(f(x_0),\ldots,f(x_i),g(x_i),\ldots,g(x_n))$ and $H_n[x]=\sum_{i=0}^n(-1)^i[T_i(x)]$, with $H_{-1}=0$ and zero lower down. Each $T_i$ is weakly increasing: monotonicity handles the two blocks and $f(x_i)\leq g(x_i)$ handles their junction. If $x_j=x_{j+1}$, then $i\leq j$ leaves the repeated pair in the $g$ block, and $i\geq j+1$ leaves it in the $f$ block. Thus every summand is repeated and $H_nD_n(P)\subseteq D_{n+1}(Q)$. The induced map on the quotients is the displayed $h_n$.

source.place: Tag 019S, lemma-homotopy-s-N, preceding equation-homotopy-to-homotopy (lines 4739–4846); explicit agent adaptation to weak tuples, quotient by repetitions, and augmentation.

proof.text: Fix $n\geq1$, and write $\delta_j$ for deleting position $j$. Expand $dH_n[x]$ into terms $(-1)^{i+j}[\delta_jT_i(x)]$. For $j<i$, one has $\delta_jT_i(x)=T_{i-1}(\delta_jx)$, whose term in $H_{n-1}d[x]$ has coefficient $(-1)^{i-1+j}$ and cancels it. For $j>i+1$, one has $\delta_jT_i(x)=T_i(\delta_{j-1}x)$, whose term in $H_{n-1}d[x]$ has coefficient $(-1)^{i+j-1}$ and cancels it. These pairings exhaust the latter sum: a term there has prism index $r\in\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$ and deleted original index $k\in\{0,\ldots,n\}$; if $k\leq r$ its partner is $(i,j)=(r+1,k)$ in the first case, while if $k>r$ its partner is $(i,j)=(r,k+1)$ in the second case.

source.place: Tag 019S, lemma-homotopy-s-N, preceding equation-homotopy-to-homotopy (lines 4739–4846); explicit agent adaptation to weak tuples, quotient by repetitions, and augmentation.

proof.text: Only $j=i$ and $j=i+1$ remain from $dH_n$. Define $A_i=(f(x_0),\ldots,f(x_{i-1}),g(x_i),\ldots,g(x_n))$ for $0\leq i\leq n+1$, with empty end blocks permitted. The $j=i$ face is $A_i$ with coefficient $(-1)^{2i}=1$; the $j=i+1$ face is $A_{i+1}$ with coefficient $(-1)^{2i+1}=-1$. Hence $dH_n[x]+H_{n-1}d[x]=\sum_{i=0}^n([A_i]-[A_{i+1}])=[g(x_0),\ldots,g(x_n)]-[f(x_0),\ldots,f(x_n)]$. This is $W(g)[x]-W(f)[x]$. Linearity gives the identity on all of $W_n(P)$, and the quotient maps of steps 2, 3 and 5 give $dh+hd=g_*-f_*$ on $C_n(P;R)$ for $n\geq1$.

proof.text: In degree zero, $H_0[x]=[f(x),g(x)]$, so $dH_0[x]=[g(x)]-[f(x)]$ and $H_{-1}d[x]=0$, even when the two vertices coincide. In degree $-1$, $d_0H_{-1}+H_{-2}d_{-1}=0$ and $W(g)_{-1}-W(f)_{-1}=\mathrm{id}_R-\mathrm{id}_R=0$. Below $-1$ all source modules vanish. Passing to the quotients proves the identity in all remaining degrees. If $P$ is empty, only the degree $-1$ check is needed; if $Q$ is empty, the assumed maps force $P$ empty. Thus no nonemptiness assumption has entered the proof.
